name: Talen Energy Corporation
industry: Independent Power Producer / Nuclear and Gas Generation
title: Talen Energy — the 1.9 GW Susquehanna AWS deal that priced AI electricity
subtitle: How a Pennsylvania nuclear and gas operator emerged from Chapter 11, signed the largest single carbon-free data center PPA in US history, and became one of the cleanest AI-electricity plays on NASDAQ
abstract: Talen Energy Corporation (TLN, NASDAQ) is a Pennsylvania-anchored independent power producer that owns and operates approximately 13.1 GW of US generation capacity — including a 90% interest in the 2.5 GW Susquehanna nuclear facility, 5.7 GW of low- and zero-carbon baseload, 2.8 GW of natural gas combined-cycle capacity acquired from Freedom and Guernsey (closed FY2025), 4.6 GW of intermediate and peaking generation, and ~800 MW of minority coal interests. The company emerged from Chapter 11 restructuring in 2023 and re-listed on NASDAQ. CEO Mark 'Mac' McFarland (joined May 2023, ex-California Resources, ex-GenOn, ex-Luminant) has executed the post-restructuring strategic refocus around long-term contracted carbon-free generation revenue. The defining commercial event was the March 2024 power purchase agreement with Amazon for Susquehanna nuclear capacity — expanded in June 2025 to up to 1,920 MW carbon-free baseload through 2042, with potential ramp to full volume by 2032, supplying Amazon's adjacent data center campus and other Pennsylvania sites. FY2025 adjusted EBITDA reached $1,035 million, adjusted FCF $524 million, and the company cleared 8,745 MW in PJM's 2027/2028 capacity auction at $333.44/MW-day. Two reliability-must-run (RMR) contracts on Brandon Shores ($145M/year) and H.A. Wagner ($35M/year) plants provide fixed annual payments through May 2029. Pending acquisitions add ~5.3 GW of gas capacity for approximately $7.25 billion total: Freedom and Guernsey (~$3.8B, closed) and Cornerstone (~$3.45B, agreed). Debt issuances of $1.4 billion 6.250% senior unsecured notes due 2034 and $1.3 billion 6.500% senior unsecured notes due 2036 fund the acquisition program; management targets net leverage around 3.5x or lower over the cycle. The board (chaired by Stephen Schaefer of GenOn Holdings and Golar LNG) pairs energy-restructuring veterans with PE-and-investment-banking executives; the executive team is heavy on nuclear (Chief Nuclear Officer Edward Casulli was Site VP at Susquehanna) and ex-Energy Future Holdings restructuring alumni. In December 2025 Talen executed a strategic management realignment: Terry Nutt was elevated to President, Cole Muller (ex-McKinsey, Wharton MBA, US Naval Academy) named CFO.
